title: Choose the look of the DeliveryFleet dispatch desk
question: The roll assigned Speed Post franking. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Speed Post Desk
options.lineage: India Post Speed Post counters: franking machines, round date postmarks, red-and-ink consignment slips
options.thesis: Every agent's work is franked: when an agent finishes, its pipeline stage receives a round postmark with agent, framework and time, so the room can see who handled the parcel and when.
materials: ruled consignment slip for the final report
tabular serial numbers (run id, order id, versions)
options.viewport: Top bar with tabs and service lamps; left column of demo cases; main area: the agent pipeline as a row of counters, each stamped as it completes; below it the zone map and the consignment slip (driver, route, ETA, outcome) side by side; event log and blackboard beneath.
options.risk: If the stamps are overused it turns into a costume; they appear only on agent completion and the final outcome.

raised.raise: A changed or blocked stage stays lit until the run ends, so nothing important flashes past the room.
Decision numbers (driver, ETA, P(on time)) set large enough to read from the back of a classroom.
All numbers share one tabular figure grammar, so columns line up across log, report and runs table.

options.label: Platform Departure Board
options.lineage: Indian Railways platform indicators and station timetables
options.thesis: Each run is a train calling at stations: the agents are stations, the live log is the timetable, and the active agent is the platform currently lit.
options.viewport: Ink header band; the pipeline as a horizontal railway line with station dots; log as a departure board below; consignment details at right.
options.risk: Most familiar of the set: transit-board dashboards are a common look, and amber-on-black dims on some projectors.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding pass + live gate board
options.thesis: The run is a boarding pass; agents update a gate board that reranks in place.
options.viewport: Pass at top with order and driver segments; board of agent rows below.
options.case: Strong on clarity (changed rows stay lit); weaker on identification for an Indian logistics project.
options.risk: Reads like a travel app rather than a fleet desk.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each stage of the run is a sign band; the next decision is always the biggest thing on screen.
options.viewport: Yellow band across the top naming the active agent; monumental ETA and driver.
options.case: Excellent from the back of a room; yellow fields are loud for a long demo.
options.risk: Yellow ground clashes with the group's crimson academic palette.

options.label: Datamatics
options.case: Strobing and density fail the projector test and the 'not flashy' rule.
options.kept: One tabular figure grammar for every number.

options.label: Dark Developer Console
options.case: Dark neon consoles are the AI-generated look you asked to avoid, and they wash out on projectors.
options.kept: Panels separated by hairline seams, not shadows; panels persist while contents change.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: One item per screen hides the pipeline, log and report the examiner must see together.
options.kept: The active run owns the first viewport; nothing else competes with it.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.case: Beautiful but unrelated to delivery; the room would not connect it to the task.
options.kept: Size of a mark carries importance, not extra text.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean logistics operations dashboard (sidebar, cards, charts) executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, KPI cards row, pipeline and log panels.
